body.text: Grahamātṛkānāmadhāraṇī
body.translated_text: The <s>Dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Grahamātṛkā</s> (Mother of the Planets)

body.text: āryagrahamātṛkā nāma dhāraṇī
body.translated_text: The <s>dhāraṇī</s> named the Noble <s>Grahamātṛkā</s>

body.text: oṃ namo bhagavatyai āryagrahamātṛkāyai /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the Blessed Lady, the Noble <s>Grahamātṛkā</s>!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān aḍakavatyāṃ mahānagaryām anekadevanāgayakṣarākṣasagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāpasmārādityasomāṅgārabudhabṛhaspatiśukraśaniścararāhuketvādibhiś cāṣṭāviṃśatinakṣatrādibhiḥ stūyamāno mahāvajrasamayālaṅkāravyūhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite siṃhāsane viharati sma / anekair bodhisattvasahasraiḥ sārdham* / tadyathā - vajrapāṇinā ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajracaṇḍena ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajrasenena ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajravināyakena ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajracāpahastena ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajravikurvitena ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajrādhipatinā ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajrālaṅkāreṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vajravikrameṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / jyotivajreṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / avalokiteśvareṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / samantabhadreṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / samantāvalokiteśvareṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / lokaśriyā ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / padmaketunā ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / ratnaketunā ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / vikasitavaktreṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / padmagarbheṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / padmanetreṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / mañjuśriyā ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / maitreyeṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the great city of <s>Aḍakavatī</s>, praised by many thousands of <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Apasmāras</s>, and by <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>Soma</s> (Moon), <s>Aṅgāra</s> (Mars), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Śaniścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, and the rest, and by the twenty-eight <s>nakṣatra</s>s (lunar mansions) and so forth — [seated] upon a lion-throne empowered by the empowerment of the array of ornaments of the great <s>vajra-samaya</s>, together with many thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Namely: with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajracaṇḍa</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajrasena</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajravināyaka</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajracāpahasta</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajravikurvita</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajrādhipati</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajrālaṅkāra</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vajravikrama</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Jyotivajra</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Samantabhadra</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Samantāvalokiteśvara</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Lokaśrī</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Padmaketu</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ratnaketu</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vikasitavaktra</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Padmagarbha</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Padmanetra</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Mañjuśrī</s>; with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> named <s>Maitreya</s>.

body.text: evaṃ pramukhair bodhisattvair mahāsattvaiḥ śatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto bhagavān dharmaṃ deśayati sma / ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ
body.translated_text: Surrounded and honored by such foremost <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the great beings, by the hundreds of thousands, the Blessed One was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> — good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end, of good meaning,

body.text: suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaparyavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma / cintāmaṇimahāvyūhālaṅkāraṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ deśayati sma / atha khalu vajrapāṇir bodhisattvo mahāsattvas tat parṣanmaṇḍalam avalokyāsanād utthāya svaṛddhyādhiṣṭhānena bhagavantam anekaśatasahasraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇamya purato niṣadya sagarveṇa paryaṅkam ābhujya līlayā tat parṣanmaṇḍalam avalokya vajrāñjalī svahṛdaye pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavantam etad avocat* / grahāś ca bhagavann ugrānugrarūpāś ca raudrāraudrarūpās ca krūrākrūrarūpāś ca sattvān viheṭhayanti / keṣāñcit prāṇam apaharanti keṣāñcid upadravāś ca kurvanti keṣāñcid ojohārāṃś ca kurvanti keṣāñcid dravyam apaharanti keṣāñcid dīrghāyuṣsattvānām alpāyuṣaṃ kurvanti / evaṃ sarvasattvānām upadraveṇa vāhayanti / tad deśayatu bhagavan dharmaparyāyaṃ yena sarvasattvānāṃ sarvopadravebhyo rakṣā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: of good wording — and he was proclaiming the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>), wholly complete, fully purified, and cleansed. He was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse named 'The Ornament of the Great Array of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel' (<s>Cintāmaṇimahāvyūhālaṅkāra</s>). Then indeed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, surveying that assembled circle, rose from his seat, and by the empowerment of his own miraculous power circumambulated the Blessed One many hundreds of thousands of times, bowed, sat down before him, proudly bent [his legs] into a cross-legged posture, surveyed that assembled circle with ease, placed the <s>vajra-añjali</s> (vajra-joined palms) at his heart, and said this to the Blessed One: 'O Blessed One, the <s>graha</s>s (planet-spirits), of fierce and ever-fiercer forms, of dreadful and ever-more-dreadful forms, of cruel and ever-crueler forms, torment beings. From some they steal away the life-breath; for some they cause calamities; for some they carry off [their] vitality (<s>ojas</s>); from some they steal away substance; for some, beings of long life, they make [the life] short. Thus they afflict all beings with calamity. Therefore, O Blessed One, may you teach a <s>Dharma</s>-discourse by which there will be protection for all beings from all calamities.'

body.text: bhagavān āha - sādhu sādhu vajrapāṇe yas tvaṃ sarvasattvānām arthāya hitāya sukhāya kṛpācittam utpādya mahāguhyātiguhyataraṃ tathāgataṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paripṛcchasi / tac chṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / grahāṇām ugrarūpāṇāṃ krūrātibhīṣaṇamukhānāṃ mahāguhyātiguhyataraṃ divyapūjām arghaṃ ca jāpañ ca dhūpañ ca -
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, in that you, having generated a mind of compassion for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of all beings, ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, [about] the great secret, the most secret of secrets. Listen to that, and attend well and properly in mind; I shall speak it to you — the great secret, the most secret of secrets: the divine worship, the offering (<s>argha</s>), the recitation (<s>jāpa</s>), and the incense, for the <s>graha</s>s of fierce forms, of cruel and most terrifying faces —'

children.translated_text: Just as, according to the difference of [each one's] description, those <s>graha</s>s are gratified,
[so], being worshipped, they are worshipped in return; [but if not,] they burn up him to whom [the offering] is brought. // 1 //

children.text: devāś cāpy asurāś caiva kinnarāś ca mahoragāḥ /
yakṣāś ca rākṣasāś caiva manuṣāś caivāmānuṣāḥ // 2 //
śamayanti ca kruddhāś ca mahānugrāś ca tejasā /
children.translated_text: when angered, they pacify with great ferocity through their power.

children.text: pūjāṃ teṣāṃ pravakṣāmi mantrāṃś cāpi yathākramam* // 3 //
children.translated_text: I shall declare their worship and <s>mantras</s> in due order. (3)

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāñ chākyamuniḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ svahṛdayāt karuṇāvikrīḍitaṃ nāma raśmijvālaṃ niścārya grahāṇāṃ mūrdhni praveśayati sma / atha tatkṣaṇād eva te sarve ādityādayo grahā utthāya bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ sarvābhir divyapūjābhiḥ pūjayitvā praṇamya jānubhir nipatya kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhūtvā bhagavantam etad avocan*
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, emitting from his own heart a blazing ray of light named <s>Karuṇāvikrīḍita</s> (Play of Compassion), caused it to enter into the crowns of the planets. Then, at that very instant, all those planets beginning with <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) rose up, worshipped the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, with all manner of divine offerings, bowed down, fell to their knees, and with palms joined together, spoke thus to the Blessed One:

body.text: anugṛhītā vayaṃ bhagavatā tathāgatenārhato samyaksaṃbuddhena tad deśayatu bhagavan tādṛśaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ yena vayaṃ sāmagrībhūtasya dharmabhāṇakasya rakṣāṃ kuryāmaḥ / guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhanaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kuryāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'We have been favored by the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. May the Blessed One teach such a <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) by which we may provide protection for a <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (dharma-preacher) who is fully assembled — guarding, safeguarding, caring, preserving, pacifying, blessing, warding off punishment, warding off weapons, counteracting poison, destroying poison, boundary-binding, and earth-binding.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāñ chākyamunis tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho grahāṇāṃ mantrapūjāñ ca bhāṣate sma / oṃ megholkāya svāhā / oṃ śītāṃśave svāhā / oṃ raktāṅgakumārāya svāhā / oṃ budhāya svāhā / oṃ bṛhaspataye svāhā / oṃ asurottamāya svāhā / oṃ kṛṣṇavarṇāya svāhā / oṃ rāhave svāhā / oṃ jyotiḥ ketave svāhā / yathānukramabhedena diśāś copadiśāś ca gandhamaṇḍalakaṃ padmamadhye dvādaśāṅgulapramāṇaṃ caturasraṃ caturdvāraṃ catustoraṇaśobhitaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ cakrasamanvitaṃ kartavyam* / tanmadhye sitakamalopari kuṅkumagandhamaṇḍalake cintayed devaṃ bhāskaraṃ tāpasarūpadharaṃ bhujābhyāṃ sitakamaladharaṃ raktavarṇaṃ sahasrasūryakoṭisamatejomālinaṃ vigraham* / asya deyaṃ kṣīrabhojanaṃ kundurudhūpam* / oṃ megholkāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, spoke the <s>mantras</s> and worship for the planets: <s>Oṃ megholkāya svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ śītāṃśave svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ raktāṅgakumārāya svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ budhāya svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bṛhaspataye svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ asurottamāya svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ kṛṣṇavarṇāya svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ rāhave svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ jyotiḥketave svāhā</s>! According to their respective order, in the cardinal and intermediate directions, a scented <s>maṇḍala</s> should be made in the center of a lotus, twelve finger-breadths in size, square, with four doors, adorned with four gateways, a palace furnished with a wheel. In the center of that, upon a white lotus, on a saffron-scented <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should visualize the deity <s>Bhāskara</s> (the Sun) bearing the form of an ascetic, holding white lotuses in both arms, red in color, a form garlanded with brilliance equal to ten million suns. To him should be offered milk food and frankincense as incense. <s>Oṃ megholkāya svāhā</s>!

body.text: pūrvasyāṃ diśi raktakamalopari priyaṅgugandhamaṇḍalake somo brāhmaṇa iti jñeyaṃ sitavarṇaṃ jaṭāmukuṭapuṣpāvasaktaṃ bhojanaghṛtodanaṃ śrīvāsadhūpaḥ / oṃ candrāmṛtavikramāya namaḥ / śītāṃśave svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the eastern direction, upon a red lotus, on a <s>priyangu</s>-scented <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Soma</s> (the Moon) should be known as a brahmin, white in color, with matted-hair crown adorned with flowers. His food offering is ghee-rice. The incense is <s>śrīvāsa</s> (pine resin). <s>Oṃ candrāmṛtavikramāya namaḥ</s>! <s>Śītāṃśave svāhā</s>!

body.text: dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi śuklakamalopari candanagandhamaṇḍalake bhikṣurūpo maṅgalo raktavarṇo ratnamakuṭo vāme śakti dakṣiṇe varadahasto bhojanam asya kṣīrabhojanaṃ bhāṣabhaktaṃ vā gugguladhūpaḥ / oṃ raktāṅgārasojjvalakumārāya namaḥ / aṅgārāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the southern direction, upon a white lotus, on a sandalwood-scented <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars) is in the form of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), red in color, with a jewel crown, holding a <s>śakti</s> (spear) in the left hand and the right hand in the boon-granting gesture. His food offering is milk food or cooked rice. The incense is <s>guggula</s> (bdellium). <s>Oṃ raktāṅgārasojjvalakumārāya namaḥ</s>! <s>Aṅgārāya svāhā</s>!

body.text: paścimāyām diśi raktapadmopari kṛṣṇāgarugandhamaṇḍalake brahmacārī budhaḥ syāt pītavarṇo raktaśmaśruḥ akṣasūtrakamaṇḍaludharaḥ / bhojanaṃ mudrabhāṣakṛṣaraḥ / dhūpo gandharasaḥ / oṃ rājaputrapītavarṇāya namaḥ / budhāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the western direction, upon a red lotus, on a black aloe-wood-scented <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) should be a <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), yellow in color, with a red beard, holding prayer beads and a water-pot. His food offering is <s>mudrā</s>-rice porridge. The incense is <s>gandharasa</s> (fragrant resin). <s>Oṃ rājaputrapītavarṇāya namaḥ</s>! <s>Budhāya svāhā</s>!

body.text: uttarasyāṃ diśi sitakamalopari devadārugandhamaṇḍalake parivrājako gurus taptakāñcanavarṇābho raktaśmaśruḥ akṣasūtrakamaṇḍaludharaḥ / asya deyaṃ dadhibhaktodanakṣīraṃ vā madhudhṛtadhūpaḥ / oṃ lohitavarṇanigamāya namaḥ bhogāspadāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the northern direction, upon a white lotus, on a <s>devadāru</s> (deodar)-scented <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is a wandering ascetic, having the complexion of molten gold, with a red beard, holding prayer beads and a water-pot. To him should be offered curd-rice or milk. The incense is honey-ghee. <s>Oṃ lohitavarṇanigamāya namaḥ bhogāspadāya svāhā</s>!

body.text: āgneyāṃ diśi raktapadmopari candanagandhamaṇḍalake śukrapāśupatadhāri gokṣīravarṇadhavalāmbho jaṭāmukutākṣasūtrakamaṇḍaludharaḥ / asya deyaṃ kṣīrabhojanaṃ karpūradhūpaḥ / oṃ namaḥ śukrādhipataye asurottamāya śuddhavigrahe svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the southeastern direction, upon a red lotus, on a sandalwood-scented <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) bears the form of a <s>Pāśupata</s> (Śaiva ascetic), white as cow's milk in complexion, with matted-hair crown, holding prayer beads and a water-pot. To him should be offered milk food. The incense is camphor. <s>Oṃ namaḥ śukrādhipataye asurottamāya śuddhavigrahe svāhā</s>!

body.text: nairṛtyāṃ diśi sitapaṅkajopari nīlacandanagandhamaṇḍalake śaniścaro kṛṣṇavarṇaphaṇabhṛtkṣapaṇako jñeyaḥ bījajaṭāmukuṭaśmaśruḥ / akṣasūtrakṣikṣirikādharo bhojanam asya bhāṣabhaktakṛṣaraḥ / dhūpo gandharasaḥ / oṃ nīlavarṇasannibhāya namaḥ / kṛṣṇaśaniścarāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the southwestern direction, upon a white lotus, on a blue sandalwood-scented <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Śaniścara</s> (Saturn) should be known as a black-colored hooded ascetic (<s>kṣapaṇaka</s>) with matted-hair crown and beard, holding prayer beads and a staff. His food offering is cooked rice porridge. The incense is <s>gandharasa</s> (fragrant resin). <s>Oṃ nīlavarṇasannibhāya namaḥ</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇaśaniścarāya svāhā</s>!

body.text: vāyavyāṃ diśi raktāmbhojopari tagarādigandhamaṇḍalake kāpāliko rāhu rājāvartanibho 'rdhadeho ravirathabhayānakalocanayugo daṃṣṭrākarālo bhṛkuṭīkṛtalalāṭapañcavarṇaḥ meghamadhyagato bhujābhyāṃ candrasūryakamalābhinayasthitaḥ / asya deyaṃ bhāṣāmiṣabhojanaṃ tilakṛṣaro vā vilvapatradhūpaḥ / oṃ vikṛtavadanarudhirāśin rāho bhṛṅgāñjanasannibhāya namaḥ / amṛtapriyāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the northwestern direction, upon a red lotus, on a fragrance-circle (<s>gandhamaṇḍalaka</s>) of <s>tagara</s> (rose-bay) and other scents, is the skull-bearing (<s>kāpālika</s>) <s>Rāhu</s>—resembling a <s>rājāvarta</s> (dark sapphire) in color, half-bodied, with a terrifying pair of eyes like the sun's chariot, fierce with fangs, with a furrowed brow and forehead of five colors, situated within a cloud, standing with both arms in the gesture of holding the moon- and sun-lotuses. His offering should be cooked meat-food or sesame-rice porridge (<s>tilakṛṣara</s>); incense of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) leaves. <s>Oṃ</s>, to the one of distorted face, drenched in blood, <s>Rāhu</s>, resembling the color of a black bee, homage! To the one fond of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: aiśānyāṃ diśi raktasaroruhopari spṛkkāgandhamaṇḍalake cāṇḍālaketur bhavet* / dhūmravarṇaḥ kṛtāñjalir nāgākṛtiḥ svapucchabhṛt* / asya deyaṃ bhojanaṃ dhṛtapūrakaṃ sajjaraso dhūpaḥ / oṃ dhūmravarṇasannibhāya jyotiṣketave namaḥ svāhā /
body.translated_text: In the northeastern direction, upon a red lotus, on a fragrance-circle of <s>spṛkkā</s> (musk) incense, is the outcaste (<s>cāṇḍāla</s>) <s>Ketu</s> (comet). He is smoke-colored, with palms joined in reverence, serpent-shaped, holding his own tail. His offering should be food of clarified-butter dumplings (<s>ghṛtapūraka</s>); incense of red arsenic (<s>sajjarasa</s>). <s>Oṃ</s>, to the one resembling smoke in color, to the banner of celestial light (<s>jyotiṣketu</s>), homage, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: maṇḍalasya pūrvadvāre buddho bhagavān dakṣiṇadvāre vajrapāṇiḥ paścimadvāre lokanāthaḥ uttaradvāre mañjuśrīkumāraḥ / pūrvottarakoṇe sarve grahāḥ pūrvadakṣiṇakoṇe sarve rāśinakṣatrāḥ dakṣiṇapaścimakoṇe sarvopadravāḥ paścimottarakoṇe bhaṭṭārikā mahāvidyā / śvetā nīlāruṇatrimukhā hastadvayena vyākhyānamudrā dakṣiṇe ratnachatrā vāme pāśaśaktidharā ratnamukuṭīvajraparyaṅkopaviṣṭā candāsanasamāsīnā ṣoḍaśavarṣākārā sarvālaṅkārabhūṣitā /
body.translated_text: At the eastern gate of the <s>maṇḍala</s> is the <s>Buddha Bhagavat</s>; at the southern gate, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>; at the western gate, <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World); at the northern gate, the youthful <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. In the northeastern corner, all the <s>grahas</s> (planets); in the southeastern corner, all the <s>rāśis</s> (zodiac signs) and <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions); in the southwestern corner, all calamities (<s>upadrava</s>); in the northwestern corner, the venerable <s>Mahāvidyā</s> (Great Spell Goddess)—white, with three faces of white, blue, and red, with two hands in the gesture of exposition (<s>vyākhyānamudrā</s>), in the right hand a jeweled parasol, in the left holding a noose and a spear (<s>śakti</s>), wearing a jeweled crown, seated in <s>vajra-paryaṅka</s> (cross-legged) posture upon a moon-seat, appearing as a sixteen-year-old maiden, adorned with all ornaments.

body.text: bāhyapūrvadvāre dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dadhibhaktaṃ dakṣiṇe virūḍhakasya dadhimāṣabhaktaṃ paścime virūpākṣasya kṣīrabhatam uttare kuberasya dadhimāṣabhaktaṃ sindūramastakam* / yathānukramabhedena puṣpādipūjā kartavyā / pratyekam dīpo deyaḥ / dhṛtamadhubhyāṃ śaṃkhaṃ pūrayitvā pañcaratnaṃ prakṣipyārgho deyaḥ / sarveṣāṃ mukhapaṭo deyam iti / evaṃ varṇabhujāsanamudrācihnāni bhavanti /
body.translated_text: At the outer eastern gate, for <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, yogurt-rice; at the southern, for <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, yogurt-and-bean-rice; at the western, for <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, milk-rice; at the northern, for <s>Kubera</s>, yogurt-and-bean-rice with vermillion on top. According to the proper sequence, offerings of flowers and so forth should be made. A lamp should be given for each. Filling a conch with clarified butter and honey, one should cast in the five jewels and offer the <s>argha</s> (water-offering). A face-cloth should be given to all. Thus are the colors, arms, seats, <s>mudrās</s>, and emblems [of the deities].

body.text: oṃ namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ sarvāśāparipūrakebhyaḥ sarvathā bhaktine svāhā / ratnatrayasya mantraṃ evaṃ pratyekaṃ japet saptasaptāṣṭaśataṃ mantram ekaikaśaḥ / evaṃ pūjitāḥ sarve grahā vividharūpiṇo dadati vipulān bhogān saubhāgyān* janayanty api /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, to all who fulfill all wishes. By all devotion, <s>svāhā</s>! One should recite the <s>mantra</s> of the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>) thus, seven times seven, one hundred and eight <s>mantras</s> each, individually. Thus worshipped, all the <s>grahas</s>, of manifold forms, grant abundant enjoyments and bring about good fortune.

body.text: imāni vajrapāṇe navagrahāṇāṃ hṛdayāni paṭhitasiddhāni tathānukramabhedena gandhamaṇḍalakaṃ kṛtvā dvādaśāṅgulimadhye pūjayitavyāni tāmramṛṇmayarūpyādibhojanena arghaṃ datvāṣṭottaraśatavārān mantraṃ japet* ekaikaśaḥ / paścāt punar vajrapāṇe gṛhamātṛkānāma dhāraṇīmantrapadāni saptavārānuccārayitavyāni / tatas te ādityādayo rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyanti / dāridryaṃ duḥkhaṃ mocayiṣyanti gatāyuṣaṃ dīrghāyuṣaṃ kariṣyanti /
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, are the heart[-mantras] of the nine <s>grahas</s>, perfected through recitation. According to the proper sequence, having made a fragrance-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should worship them within [a space of] twelve finger-breadths, and having given the <s>argha</s> offering with copper, clay, or silver food-vessels, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> one hundred and eight times each. Afterwards, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>dhāraṇī-mantra</s> words called <s>Gṛhamātṛkā</s> should be recited seven times. Then those [planets] beginning with <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) will provide protection, shelter, and guardianship. They will liberate from poverty and suffering, and will make those whose life-span has expired live long.

body.text:
yaś ca khalu punar vajrapāṇe bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikān ye vā sattvajātīyā yeṣāṃ karṇapuṭe śabdaṃ nipatiṣyanti na teṣām akālamṛtyunā kālaṃ kariṣyanti / yaś ca khalu punar vajrapāṇe grahān maṇḍalamadhye pūjayitvā dine dine saptavārānuccārayiṣyanti / tatra
tasya dharmabhāṇakasya sarve grahāḥ sarveṇa sarvāśāṃ paripūrayiṣyanti / tatkulād api dāridryañ ca nāśāyiṣyanti /
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, whatever <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, <s>upāsikās</s>, or whatever beings in whose ears these words shall fall—they shall not die by untimely death. And moreover, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, whoever, having worshipped the <s>grahas</s> in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, shall recite [the dhāraṇī] seven times every day—for that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma), all the <s>grahas</s> will completely fulfill all wishes. And they will destroy poverty even from his family.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāñ chākyamuni tathāgataḥ punar api gṛhamātṛkānāma dhāraṇīmantrapadāni bhāṣate sma / oṃ namo ratnatrayāya / oṃ namo buddhāya / oṃ namo dharmāya / oṃ namaḥ saṃghāya / oṃ namo vajradharāya / oṃ namaḥ padmadharāya / oṃ namaḥ kumārāya / oṃ namaḥ sarvagrahāṇāṃ sarvāśāparipūrakāṇām* / oṃ namaḥ nakṣatrāṇām* / oṃ namo dvādaśarāśīnām* / oṃ namaḥ sarvopadravāṇām* / tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> once again spoke the <s>dhāraṇī-mantra</s> words called <s>Gṛhamātṛkā</s>: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>)! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Vajradhara</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Padmadhara</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the Youth (<s>Kumāra</s>)! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to all the <s>grahas</s> who fulfill all wishes! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the <s>nakṣatras</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the twelve <s>rāśis</s> (zodiac signs)! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to all calamities! That is to say—

body.text: oṃ buddhe 2 śuddhe 2 vajre 2 padme 2 sara 2 prasare 2 smara 2 krīḍa 2 krīḍaya 2 mara 2 māraya 2 mardaya 2 stambha 2 stambhaya 2 ghaṭa 2 ghāṭaya 2 mama sarvasattvānāñ ca vighnān* chinda chinda bhinda 2 sarvavighnān nāśanaṃ kuru 2 mama saparivārasya sarvasattvānāñ ca kāryaṃ kṣepaya 2 mama sarvasattvānāñ ca sarvanakṣatragrahapīḍān nivāraya 2 bhagavati śriyaṃ kuru mahāmāyā prasādhaya sarvaduṣṭān nāśaya sarvapāpāni mama saparivārasya sarvasattvānāñ ca rakṣa 2 vajre 2 caṇḍe 2 caṇḍini 2 nuru 2 musu 2 mumu 2 muñca 2 havā have ugre ugratare pūraya bhagavati manorathaṃ mama sarvaparivārasya sarvasattvānāñ ca sarvatathāgatādiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite svāhā / oṃ svāhā / hūṃ svāhā / hrīḥ svāhā / dhūḥ svāhā / dhīḥ svāhā / oṃ ādityāya svāhā / oṃ somāya svāhā / oṃ dharaṇīsutāya svāhā / oṃ budhāya svāhā / oṃ bṛhaspataye svāhā / oṃ śukrāya svāhā / oṃ śaniścarāya svāhā / oṃ rāhave svāhā / oṃ ketave svāhā / oṃ buddhāya svāhā / oṃ vajrapāṇaye svāhā / oṃ padmadharāya svāhā / oṃ kumārāya svāhā / oṃ sarvagrahāṇāṃ svāhā / oṃ sarvanakṣatrāṇāṃ svāhā / sarvopadravāṇāṃ svāhā / oṃ dvādaśarāśīnāṃ svāhā / oṃ sarvavidye hūṃ 2 phaṭ* svāhā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ buddhe buddhe, śuddhe śuddhe, vajre vajre, padme padme, sara sara, prasara prasara, smara smara, krīḍa krīḍa, krīḍaya krīḍaya, mara mara, māraya māraya, mardaya mardaya, stambha stambha, stambhaya stambhaya, ghaṭa ghaṭa, ghāṭaya ghāṭaya — cut, cut, pierce, pierce all obstacles of me and all beings, destroy all obstacles, accomplish, accomplish the task of me together with my retinue and all beings, swiftly, swiftly! Ward off, ward off all afflictions of <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) and <s>grahas</s> (planets) for me and all beings! O Blessed One, bestow prosperity! O <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (Great Illusion), accomplish! Destroy all evil beings! Protect, protect me together with my retinue and all beings from all sins! Vajre vajre, caṇḍe caṇḍe, caṇḍini caṇḍini, nuru nuru, musu musu, mumu mumu, muñca muñca, havā have, O fierce one, O most fierce one — fulfill, O Blessed One, the heart's desire of me together with my entire retinue and all beings, empowered by the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ <s>svāhā</s>! Hūṃ <s>svāhā</s>! Hrīḥ <s>svāhā</s>! Dhūḥ <s>svāhā</s>! Dhīḥ <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Soma</s> (the Moon) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Dharaṇīsuta</s> (Mars, Son of the Earth) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Śaniścara</s> (Saturn) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Rāhu</s> <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Ketu</s> <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to the <s>Buddha</s> <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to the Lotus-Bearer (<s>Padmadhara</s>) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to <s>Kumāra</s> <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to all <s>grahas</s> <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to all <s>nakṣatras</s> <s>svāhā</s>! To all calamities <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ to the twelve <s>rāśis</s> (zodiac signs) <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ sarvavidye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: imāni vajrapāṇe grahamātṛkānāma dhāraṇīmantrapadāni sarvasiddhikarāṇi ca / yac ca khalu punar vajrapāṇe imāni grahamātṛkānāma dhāraṇīmantrapadāni kārtikamāsaśuklapakṣasya saptamīm ārabhyopoṣadhiko bhūtvā yāvac caturdaśīgrahanakṣatrān madhye pūjayitvā dine dine saptavārānuccārayitavyāni / tataḥ pūrṇamāsyām ahorātraṃ vācayet* / tasya navanavativarṣāṇi mṛtyubhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / ulkāpātagrahanakṣatrapīḍābhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / jātau jātau jātismaro bhaviṣyati / sarve grahā īpsitaṃ varaṃ dāsyanti /
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, are the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> syllables called <s>Grahamātṛkā</s> (Mother of Planets), which accomplish all <s>siddhis</s> (attainments). Furthermore, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, these <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> syllables called <s>Grahamātṛkā</s> should be recited as follows: beginning on the seventh day of the bright half of the month of <s>Kārtika</s>, having observed the <s>upoṣadha</s> (fasting) vow, one should worship the planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> in the midst until the fourteenth day, and recite [the dhāraṇī] seven times each day. Then on the full moon day, one should recite it day and night. For that person, there will be no fear of death for ninety-nine years. There will be no fear from the afflictions of falling meteors, planets, or <s>nakṣatras</s>. In birth after birth, one will possess memory of past lives (<s>jātismara</s>). All the planets will grant the desired boon.

body.text: atha te sarve grahāḥ sādhu bhagavann iti kṛtvā praṇamyāntarhitābhūvann iti / idam avocad bhagavān āttamanās te ca bhikṣavas te ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatīparṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti /
body.translated_text: Then all those planets, saying "Excellent, O Blessed One!" bowed down and disappeared. This the Blessed One spoke, and those <s>bhikṣus</s>, those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, and that entire assembly, together with the world of <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

body.text: āryagrahamātṛkānāma dhāraṇī samāptā //
body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Grahamātṛkā</s> (Mother of Planets) is complete.
